record.paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
record.original_question: For the delayed constant-yield harvesting equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) - h, where h > 0 and the recruitment function f is continuous, decreasing, satisfies f(0) = b > 1, and makes x f(x) increasing and bounded, is the largest persisting set D_h monotone decreasing as the harvesting quota h increases? Equivalently, if h_1 <= h_2, must every initial condition whose solution persists under harvesting level h_2 also persist under harvesting level h_1, so that D_{h_2} is a subset of D_{h_1}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuous, decreasing function with $f(0)=b>1$ such that the map $x\mapsto xf(x)$ is increasing and bounded on $[0,\infty)$. For a parameter $h>0$, consider the second-order difference equation with delayed constant-yield harvesting
$$x_{n+1}=x_n f(x_{n-1})-h,\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots,$$
with initial conditions $(x_{-1},x_0)\in[0,\infty)^2$. Say that a solution persists if $x_n\ge 0$ for all $n\ge 0$ and the sequence does not become negative or extinct in finite time. Let
$$D_h=\{(x_{-1},x_0)\in[0,\infty)^2 : \text{the solution with these initial conditions persists}\}$$
be the largest persisting set for harvesting level $h$.

Prove or disprove: $D_h$ is monotone decreasing in $h$; that is, for all $0<h_1\le h_2$ one has $D_{h_2}\subseteq D_{h_1}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears in a 2016 study on harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models and is explicitly listed among that work's open problems/conjectures. A 2017 follow-up paper studies the related constant-effort harvesting model but does not appear to resolve this specific monotonicity conjecture for the delayed constant-yield case. No source found that proves or disproves it.
